newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Richemont sees Rothmans sales slowing in H2.
newsitem.headline: Richemont sees Rothmans sales slowing in H2.

text.p: Luxury goods holding Compagnie Financiere Richemont AG said it expected the pace of growth in sales of Rothmans International to slow in the second half due to gains in sterling on the foreign exchange market.

"It is expected that the trading results of Rothmans International for the year to March 1997 will be satisfactory. The rate of growth achieved in the first six months is unlikely to be maintained, however, due to the strengthening of sterling," the company said in a statement presenting results for the first half of its business year.

Richemont said operating profit for the six month to September 30 rose 31.7 percent to 466.2 million pounds from 354.1 million a year earlier. Net sales grew 15 percent to 2,343 million pounds from 2,037 million.
Overall, it said it expected the group's profitability to be maintained.
"We believe that the group's overall profitability for the current financial year as a whole will continue to reflect the trend seen in the first six months of the year," Richemont said.
It said expected the results for its Vendome luxury goods subsidiary to improve.

"Vendome's results for the second half of the previous financial year were affected by several unfavourable external events, which had a significant effect on the results in the important pre-Christmas period. Provided such unfavourable events do not recur, it is anticipated that the Group's luxury goods interests will show increases in sales revenues and operating profits in Swiss franc terms in the remainder of this year," Richemont said.
With respect to its media interests, it said that the merger of NetHold and Canal+ was not expected to be completed until the final quarter of the current financial year.

"The group's results for the remainder of the year will therefore reflect the planned costs of further developing NetHold's business, in particular in relation to the introduction of digital technology and sports channels in a number of European and African markets," Richemont said.

In a note provided with its earnings, it said that the merger of NetHold's European operations with those of Canal+ was likely only to be completed at the end of the current financial year, and was thus unlikely to be reflected in its earnings for the ongoing business year.
